summary: Modern data platforms have embedded AI/ML directly into the database layer, letting developers run inference, generate embeddings, and perform semantic search via SQL without exporting data to separate ML systems. Capabilities range from native vector search and managed LLM functions (Snowflake Cortex, BigQuery ML, Databricks Mosaic AI, MongoDB Atlas) to extension-based or external-model approaches (PostgreSQL pgvector/pgai, Aurora ML, Redshift ML). Vector-based retrieval is becoming foundational for GenAI, with Gartner projecting 30% of enterprises will rely on it by 2026 and the vector database market forecast to reach ~$17.9B by 2034.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (serverless LLM & ML functions)
databases.description: Cortex provides SQL-callable functions for LLM tasks (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EXTRACT_ANSWER), embedding generation, and Cortex Search for RAG. It hosts managed foundation models (e.g., from Anthropic, Meta, Mistral) and offers Cortex Analyst for natural-language-to-SQL. Snowflake also extends Cortex into its managed Postgres offering.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a VECTOR data type, VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY/L2/INNER_PRODUCT functions, and Cortex Search as a managed hybrid vector+keyword retrieval service built directly into the platform.
databases.llm_integration: Built-in managed access to foundation models (Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic) callable via SQL/Python; no external API keys required.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based; Cortex functions billed per token/credit based on model and usage, on top of standard Snowflake compute (credits) and storage.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets you create, train, and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time series, etc.) using SQL. Through remote models it connects to Vertex AI foundation models for text generation, embeddings (ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING), and generative tasks (ML.GENERATE_TEXT) directly in SQL.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery supports a VECTOR_SEARCH function and CREATE VECTOR INDEX for approximate nearest-neighbor search over embeddings stored in tables.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI (Gemini, PaLM, text-embedding models) via remote models and endpoints invoked from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Pay-per-query (bytes scanned) or capacity-based slots for BigQuery; Vertex AI model calls and embedding generation billed separately by Vertex AI pricing.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector extension plus pgai for in-database AI
databases.description: pgvector adds a vector column type and similarity operators to PostgreSQL, while pgai (from Timescale) adds SQL functions to call external LLMs/embedding APIs (OpenAI, Cohere, Ollama, etc.) and automate embedding pipelines (pgai Vectorizer). Together they enable storing, generating, and searching embeddings within standard Postgres.
databases.vector_search_notes: Extension-based, not core. Vector search is provided by the pgvector extension (HNSW and IVFFlat indexes), which must be installed; vanilla PostgreSQL has no native vector type. On managed Postgres it is native only where the provider ships pgvector.
databases.llm_integration: Via pgai, which calls external LLM/embedding provider APIs from SQL; also commonly paired with LangChain for RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Open source and free; costs are infrastructure/hosting plus any external LLM API usage. No per-feature licensing.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you add ML-based predictions to applications using SQL by integrating Aurora with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock/Comprehend. You call ML models via SQL functions to run inference (e.g., sentiment, custom SageMaker models, Bedrock text/embedding models) on data in the database.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to Aurora ML. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL requires the pgvector extension; Aurora ML itself provides model inference, not a built-in vector index.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker-hosted models, plus Comprehend, invoked through SQL functions.
databases.pricing_notes: No extra charge for the Aurora ML feature itself; you pay standard Aurora costs plus the underlying SageMaker/Bedrock/Comprehend inference charges.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.description: Redshift ML allows users to create, train, and deploy ML models using the CREATE MODEL SQL command, powered by Amazon SageMaker (Autopilot and custom models). It also supports calling external LLMs via Amazon Bedrock and running predictions directly in SQL queries over warehouse data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native. Redshift ML focuses on model training/inference; it does not provide a built-in ANN vector index. Vector workloads typically require external services or other AWS databases.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock (generative models) invoked from SQL for prediction and generative tasks.
databases.pricing_notes: No additional Redshift ML charge for using the feature with local training within limits; you pay for SageMaker training/inference and Bedrock usage plus standard Redshift compute/storage.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI platform with Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Mosaic AI provides end-to-end GenAI tooling on the Lakehouse: model training/fine-tuning, model serving, Foundation Model APIs, AI functions in SQL (ai_query, ai_gen), agent frameworks, and governance via Unity Catalog. Databricks Vector Search offers a managed, serverless vector index synced to Delta tables.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in managed service that automatically syncs and indexes embeddings from Delta tables for low-latency similarity search.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Foundation Model APIs and Model Serving host open and proprietary LLMs; supports external model endpoints (OpenAI, Anthropic) and fine-tuning, callable via SQL AI functions and MLflow.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based (DBUs) for compute and model serving; Vector Search and Foundation Model APIs billed by usage (compute/tokens) on top of standard Databricks pricing.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search (native vector search in the document database)
databases.description: Atlas Vector Search lets you store embeddings alongside operational JSON documents and run approximate nearest-neighbor queries using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage. It supports hybrid search combining vector, full-text, and metadata filters, enabling RAG directly over operational data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Vector search is built into Atlas via dedicated vector search indexes and the $vectorSearch operator (HNSW-based ANN), with no third-party extension required.
databases.llm_integration: No bundled proprietary LLM; integrates with external providers (OpenAI, Cohere, Voyage AI, Amazon Bedrock, Azure OpenAI) and frameworks like LangChain/LlamaIndex for embeddings and RAG.
databases.pricing_notes: Available on Atlas dedicated tiers; vector search runs on Search Nodes (or cluster resources) billed as part of Atlas consumption/instance pricing. External embedding/LLM costs are separate.
